summary: This work presents a scalable parallel neural network decoder for surface codes that achieves state-of-the-art accuracy while enabling real-time decoding throughput by training a recurrent transformer to output local logical corrections per decoding window that self-coordinate across boundaries. A single TPU v6e achieves <1 μs per syndrome round for surface codes up to distance 25, compared to AlphaQubit's ~20 μs latency, validated experimentally on the Zuchongzhi 3.2 superconducting processor achieving logical error rates of 0.0078 ± 0.0001 per round at d=7.
motivation: AlphaQubit-type neural decoders exceed traditional decoders like MWPM in accuracy but incur 20–48 μs latency per syndrome round, far exceeding the ~1 μs throughput requirement for real-time fault-tolerant quantum computation on superconducting platforms. Existing parallel decoders require local physical error corrections at window seams, incompatible with AlphaQubit's global logical output.
method: A recurrent transformer architecture processes syndrome windows with buffer regions (size d) and core regions (size d), trained jointly across initial, bulk, and final window types. Ground truth labels $y_i = |\mathcal{E} \cap E_i^c \cap L| \bmod 2$ are derived from consistent error sets, enabling self-coordination. Multi-layer recurrent training (Eq. 4) with truncated core sizes, DEM-based fine-tuning, and end-to-end optimization via differentiable Soft-XOR (Eq. 5) complete the framework.
result: On Zuchongzhi 3.2, per-round logical error rates are 0.01451 ± 0.00004 (d=3), 0.00971 ± 0.00005 (d=5), and 0.00783 ± 0.0001 (d=7), outperforming PyMatching, Belief-Matching, and Correlated-Matching. Fault-tolerance threshold reaches 0.76% versus 0.62% for MWPM. Throughput scales to d=25 at 0.979 ± 0.021 μs per round on TPU v6e, sustaining constant latency for arbitrarily long memory experiments.
